turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, so what brings me in... well, it’s mostly this constant restless feeling I’ve been having. It’s like I’m just wound way too tight and I can’t fully settle down. 

Even when I’m supposed to be calmly sitting through a planning meeting at work—I'm a retail buyer, actually, and right now we're looking at the fall vendor catalogs, which honestly have been so delayed this year because of all those global shipping issues. It's been a total headache trying to get the seasonal displays coordinated, especially the home goods section. 

But anyway, yeah, even in those meetings, or... or even when I'm doing things that are supposed to be relaxing, like painting or doing yoga. I just can't settle. My yoga instructor has this beautiful studio downtown with all these huge ferns, and she's always telling me to just sink into the mat and find my center, but I'm just sitting there feeling like a coiled spring instead.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly reports a 'constant restless feeling' and an inability to settle down.
symptom_reasoning.S013: The patient describes being unable to settle during relaxing leisure activities like painting and yoga.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient describes feeling 'wound way too tight' and like a 'coiled spring,' indicating physical tension and feeling keyed up.

turns.doctor_question: Beyond this feeling of being restless or 'wound up,' have you also been experiencing a persistent low mood or a loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
Low mood? Um, no, not really. I still definitely enjoy my hobbies and everything. Like the painting I mentioned, I actually just started this big new watercolor piece last weekend. I had to go to this little art supply shop down on 4th Street to get a specific size of flat brush, and they had completely redone their entire store layout. 

It was driving me crazy because, you know, being in retail myself, I absolutely cannot help but analyze how people merchandise their spaces. They put all these heavy, clunky wooden easels right next to the delicate watercolor paper pads, which is just a total disaster waiting to happen if a customer bumps the display. I actually almost said something to the manager because it was just so poorly thought out, but... wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? 

Oh, right, feeling sad or losing interest. No, no, I don't feel depressed or anything like that. I still want to do things, I just have that... constantly revved up feeling while I'm doing them.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by unrelated thoughts about an art supply store and forgets the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes having a 'constantly revved up feeling,' which aligns with acting as if driven by a motor.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies having a low mood or feeling depressed.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies losing interest, stating they still definitely enjoy their hobbies and want to do things.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel this 'revved up' sensation, do you often find yourself worrying excessively about a wide range of different things, like your health, your finances, or your performance at work?
turns.patient_response:
Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I care about my job and everything, obviously, but I don't sit around agonizing over things. Like, my finances are fine. I actually just switched banks last month because my old one—well, they got bought out by this massive national chain, and suddenly all the tellers I knew were gone. 

There was this one teller, Brenda, who always used to give my dog a treat when we went through the drive-thru. She had this little jar of those peanut butter biscuits. My dog, Buster, he’s a terrier mix, and he would just go absolutely nuts the second we pulled into the parking lot. He knew exactly where we were. But anyway, the new bank doesn't do that, and they changed all the online banking interfaces, which is just so frustrating. It’s like they didn't even test it with real users. 

But no, I don't worry excessively. It's not anxiety, it's just... physical energy, you know? Like I just need to be moving.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes having physical energy and feeling a constant need to be moving, which indicates restlessness.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying excessively or agonizing over things like finances or work.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your life, have you felt this same restless, 'revved up' energy ever since you were a child, or is this something that only started more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, it's definitely been my whole life. I mean, way back in elementary school, I remember my parents getting notes sent home all the time because I just kept popping out of my seat. Those seats back then, they had those desks where the chair is actually attached to the desk part with that heavy metal bar? I don't know if you had those. They were so uncomfortable, especially in the spring when you'd wear shorts and your legs would just stick to the plastic. I went to this older school building that didn't even have air conditioning, which is just wild to think about now. 

But yeah, I just couldn't stay in those seats. And the notes also said I was always talking over my classmates, or I'd be rushing to shout out the answer before the teacher even finished asking the question. My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she used to get so flustered with me. She had this massive collection of ceramic frogs on her desk. Literally everywhere, just frogs. If you brought her a frog trinket, you got a special sticker or something, which looking back seems a little weird, right? Like, why so many frogs? I always wondered where she kept them all during the summer. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, right, if it started recently. No, yeah, it's not a new thing at all. I've always had this kind of energy.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts, going on tangents about school desks and ceramic frogs before forgetting the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient recalls getting notes sent home because they 'kept popping out of my seat' and 'couldn't stay in those seats'.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient confirms the doctor's description of having a restless, 'revved up' energy, stating they have 'always had this kind of energy'.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient explicitly states they would rush to shout out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient mentions that they were 'always talking over my classmates', indicating interrupting and intruding on others.
